A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 28-page versions of the same RAM paper. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover the main text, figures, tables, equations, Appendices A–F, and checklist. The reordered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original Llama3 and Qwen2.5 experiments, ablations, and supplementary comparisons, including benchmark results in Tables 3–4 and latency measurements in Appendix F.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and supplementary results, including the revised baseline latency measurement in Table 12.

M1.justification: The RAM factorization, sequence-level training objective, Proposing-Aligning-Reducing Sampling procedure, and KL-divergence fallback remain unchanged in Section 2 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same UltraChat instruction-following, TL;DR summarization, Anthropic-HH helpfulness/harmlessness, and AlpacaEval 2 evaluation coverage. No datasets or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same warmed-up, SFT, DPO, Aligner, and Controlled Decoding baselines in Tables 3–4 and Appendix F. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The stated model configurations, training settings, evaluation samples, judges, and prompts are unchanged. Table 12 retains 126 input tokens; no revised timing procedure accompanies its numerical update.

E4.justification: Section 5 retains the same aligner-size and alpha sensitivity analyses and training-efficiency comparison. Appendix F retains the output-length analysis and latency comparison without adding or removing an analytical question.

E5.justification: Figures 2–3 retain their error bars, and Section 5 retains the same standard-deviation and coefficient-of-variation reporting. No run counts, seeds, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 12 changes Llama8B+Ali. 1B first-token latency from 50.72 seconds to 10.14 seconds under unchanged reported settings. RAM remains at 0.31 seconds, and the other results are unchanged. This localized revision reduces RAM's reported latency advantage without changing the ranking.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, training derivations, Proposition 2.1, and its Appendix B proof are unchanged. The grammatical correction preceding Equation 7 does not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about detachable alignment through importance sampling, efficient sequence-level training, low-latency token decoding, and empirical performance.

C2.justification: The variance-reduction explanation, Aligner distribution-mismatch interpretation, Controlled Decoding discussion, and Appendix A vocabulary limitations are unchanged. Appendix F.2 retains its interpretation despite the revised latency value.

D1.justification: Appendices C–E retain the same implementation instructions, hyperparameters, optimizer, and evaluation prompts. Hardware disclosures and checklist statements about code and data availability are also unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds four introductory citations: work on bias unlearning, FlipGuard, LIRE, and principle-guided decoding, numbered 23 and 43–45. The related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged; other citation differences are renumbering.

P1.justification: v4 corrects 'we transforms' to 'we transform' in Section 2.3 and moves the checklist from after Appendices A–F to before them. The main narrative otherwise remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded bibliography changes reference-page layout, and the checklist and appendix blocks exchange positions. Figures and tables retain their designs and captions; Table 12's numerical revision does not change its display structure.

improvement.justification: The added citations and small editorial changes leave overall clarity and scientific substance essentially unchanged. Table 12 revises Aligner latency from 50.72 to 10.14 seconds while preserving RAM's latency advantage, but provides no explanation establishing improved measurement accuracy. The revision leaves the paper's methodological rigor, empirical coverage, and reproducibility information essentially unchanged.
